questions.stem: Describe the sequence of stages in the instruction execution cycle and explain the purpose of each stage.
markingGuide: Fetch: Retrieve the instruction from memory.
Decode: Interpret the instruction and its operands.
Execute: Perform the operation specified by the instruction.
Memory Access: Access memory if needed for the instruction.
Write-back: Store the result back to a register or memory.
questions.explanation: The instruction execution cycle consists of five stages: fetch, decode, execute, memory access, and write-back. Each stage has a specific purpose, from retrieving the instruction to storing the result. Understanding each stage is crucial for comprehending how a CPU executes instructions.
